title: Iran fires missiles at the Al Udeid air base in Qatar
body:
On 23 June 2025, at about 19:39 local time, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps fired missiles at Al Udeid Air Base near Doha, Qatar, the regional headquarters of US Central Command. It was Iran's retaliation for the US strikes on its nuclear sites on 22 June. The IRGC said it was one missile for each US bomb dropped.

The figures differ by source. Iran said it fired 14 missiles and that 6 hit the base. Qatar said it intercepted 13 missiles and that one impacted, and a US official said 13 were intercepted and one was allowed to crash harmlessly off target. Qatar and the United States reported no casualties. Satellite imagery showed damage to a radar dome, and a Pentagon spokesperson confirmed a missile struck it. Iran warned Qatar and the US hours before the attack.

President Donald Trump called the attack a "very weak response" and thanked Iran for the early notice, and hours later he announced a ceasefire proposal. Qatar condemned the attack, said it reserved the right to respond, summoned Iran's ambassador on 24 June and wrote to the UN Security Council. Iran described the strike as self-defence unrelated to Qatar, which it called a friendly neighbour. Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt, Jordan and Turkey condemned it, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said he was deeply alarmed, and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the response proportionate.
